nodes.label: Real-time Latency
nodes.rationale: The repository's highest-priority goal is stage-level latency measured and published as p50, p99, and p99.9.

nodes.label: Order-book Correctness
nodes.rationale: The local order book must never silently drift; sequence gaps trigger automatic resynchronization.

nodes.label: Honest Backtesting
nodes.rationale: Backtests model fees, slippage, and latency, and recorded days replay identically.

nodes.label: Fixed-point Boundary Rule
nodes.rationale: Money and quantities cannot cross boundaries as floating point values; each stack uses an exact representation.

nodes.label: Single Rust Order-book Implementation
nodes.rationale: Python uses the Rust order book through PyO3 and neither Python nor Java may reimplement it, preventing behavioral drift.

nodes.label: Paper Trading Only
nodes.rationale: The application must never place real orders or access real funds or brokerage credentials.

nodes.label: Token Security
nodes.rationale: Access tokens are short-lived EdDSA JWTs with key identifiers, while opaque refresh tokens are SHA-256 stored, rotated, and reuse-detected.

nodes.label: Per-user Data Isolation
nodes.rationale: Every user-owned query is filtered by user_id.

nodes.label: Protobuf Service Contracts
nodes.rationale: Protobuf plus gRPC provides typed, versioned streaming contracts, and proto is the source of truth.

nodes.label: Bounded Queue Conflation
nodes.rationale: Market data queues conflate to the latest state on overflow; command queues reject, avoiding unbounded buffering.

nodes.label: PyO3 Shared Rust Book
nodes.rationale: PyO3 and maturin let research use one order-book implementation; an independent Numba implementation risks drift.

nodes.label: Single Writer per Account
nodes.rationale: Paper-trading commands are serialized by account to prevent overspending.

nodes.label: Conservative Resting Limit Model
nodes.rationale: Resting limits fill only on a qualifying through-trade, never a touch or quote movement, because queue position is unknown.

nodes.label: Backtesting Execution Model
nodes.rationale: Recorded events are replayed through the same Rust book as live operation so backtests do not approximate market structure differently.

nodes.label: No-Lookahead Guard
nodes.rationale: The engine, rather than a convention, prevents future data from being exposed to strategies.

nodes.label: Live Paper-Trading Parity
nodes.rationale: Shared golden vectors and a parity test ensure backtest fills, fees, latency rules, and ledger balances match Java paper trading.

nodes.label: Authentication and Session Security
nodes.rationale: Short-lived signed access tokens, rotating hashed refresh tokens, and secure browser storage limit account takeover and token theft.

nodes.label: Authorization and Tenant Isolation
nodes.rationale: Repositories explicitly scope every user-owned query by the authenticated user ID, with isolation tests for each resource.

nodes.label: Deterministic Replay Testing
nodes.rationale: Recorded input is replayed through Rust, PyO3, and Java paths to verify identical books, metrics, fills, and ledgers.

nodes.label: Property and Differential Testing
nodes.rationale: Components with simple references, especially the order book and fill model, are validated by properties and differential vectors.

nodes.label: Latency Measurement and Observability
nodes.rationale: The system uses staged timestamps, same-clock headline measurements, percentile reporting, and Prometheus metrics to make latency claims auditable.

nodes.label: Docker Compose Profiles
nodes.rationale: Profiles let a local developer start only the infrastructure and application services needed for a task.

nodes.label: CI/CD Workflow Design
nodes.rationale: Path-filtered, detect-gated workflows keep the monorepo's per-language checks fast while preserving required quality and security gates.

nodes.label: Linux Filesystem Benchmark Requirement
nodes.rationale: Published benchmarks must be produced on a Linux filesystem because NTFS and OneDrive builds are slower or noisier and undermine credible performance results.

nodes.label: Phase-Gated Delivery
nodes.rationale: A phase cannot begin until the preceding phase's measurable exit criteria are met, protecting latency and correctness work from scope creep.

nodes.label: Project Risk Management
nodes.rationale: Risks are scored by likelihood and impact, paired with early signals and mitigations, and reviewed at the start of every phase.

nodes.label: ADR-0001: Polyglot Split
nodes.rationale: Rust owns the low-latency feed, Java the product API, Python research and backtesting, and Next.js the frontend so each domain uses its natural language fit.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: Direct gRPC Live Path
nodes.rationale: A direct Rust-to-Java gRPC stream minimizes live-path hops and operational weight; the message bus remains optional for later consumers.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: Fixed-Point Integers
nodes.rationale: Scaled integers keep prices, quantities, balances, fills, and fees exact and deterministic across boundaries; floating point is restricted to derived analytics.

nodes.label: ADR-0004: Optimized Book with Oracle
nodes.rationale: A dense optimized order book pursues hot-path speed while a BTreeMap oracle and differential properties preserve correctness.

nodes.label: ADR-0005: PyO3 Shared Book
nodes.rationale: The Rust book, metrics, and event reader are exposed to Python in coarse batches to avoid divergent live and backtest implementations.

nodes.label: ADR-0006: Event Log Format
nodes.rationale: Framed Protobuf plus zstd supports cheap lossless hot-path appends and replay, while compaction to Parquet serves columnar research.

nodes.label: ADR-0007: JWT and Rotating Refresh Tokens
nodes.rationale: Short-lived asymmetric JWTs and reuse-detecting rotating refresh tokens combine stateless hot-path validation with session revocation and theft detection.

nodes.label: ADR-0008: Client-Only Next.js Live App
nodes.rationale: The static marketing site and client-only live application share Next.js while the browser connects directly to Java WebSocket to avoid a proxy hop.

nodes.label: ADR-0009: Paper Trading Only
nodes.rationale: Simulating trades against live books avoids real-money, custody, investment-advice, and brokerage obligations without diluting the engineering goals.

nodes.label: ADR-0010: JSON WebSocket v1
nodes.rationale: Compact JSON is native to browsers and easy to debug for v1; a future binary Protobuf protocol is reserved if measured browser parse cost warrants it.

nodes.label: ADR-0011: Proto Codegen Strategy
nodes.rationale: Buf provides pinned schema linting, formatting, builds, and breaking checks, while native language build tools generate code without committing generated artifacts.

nodes.label: ADR-0012: sb- Crate Name Prefix
nodes.rationale: The sb- prefix avoids collision and import ambiguity with Rust's built-in core crate while retaining stable architecture directory names.

nodes.label: Polyglot Architecture
nodes.rationale: Accepted ADR 0001 splits the platform across Rust, Java, Python, and Next.js.

nodes.label: Direct gRPC Live Path
nodes.rationale: Accepted ADR 0002 makes the message bus optional.

nodes.label: Fixed-Point Integers
nodes.rationale: Accepted ADR 0003 requires fixed-point integers across all boundaries.

nodes.label: JWT Access and Rotating Refresh Tokens
nodes.rationale: Accepted ADR 0007 establishes multi-user authentication with JWT access and rotating refresh tokens.

nodes.label: Paper Trading Only
nodes.rationale: Accepted ADR 0009 limits the platform to paper trading.

nodes.label: WebSocket Web Worker
nodes.rationale: Messages are batched in a Web Worker and delivered at animation-frame rate before Zustand handlers update client state.

nodes.label: Refresh Token Cookie Authentication
nodes.rationale: The access token is kept in memory while the refresh token is held in an httpOnly cookie.

nodes.label: Docker Secrets
nodes.rationale: JWT keys and other secrets are mounted as Docker secrets rather than kept in Compose files.

nodes.label: Permissive Development CORS
nodes.rationale: The development profile permits all origins for CORS.

nodes.label: Shared Subscribe Request
nodes.rationale: Buf lint exceptions preserve a shared SubscribeRequest and domain-specific responses for the MarketData service.

nodes.label: Authority Notification
nodes.rationale: The runbook sets a six-hour CERT-In deadline and a 72-hour GDPR deadline when applicable.

nodes.label: Layered DDoS Defense
nodes.rationale: The defense layers are Cloudflare or AWS Shield, NGINX or Envoy, Java rate limiting, and service-level protection.

nodes.label: JWT Key Rotation
nodes.rationale: JWT access-key compromise requires a new EdDSA keypair, a rolling API restart, invalidation of existing access tokens, and refresh-token rotation.

nodes.label: Incident Response Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: The runbook prescribes detection and triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident work.

nodes.label: Development Helpers
nodes.rationale: Helpers are required to be idempotent and documented at the top of each file.

nodes.label: Skills Index
nodes.rationale: A matching skill must be loaded before working in its area; project specifications and ADRs take precedence over a conflicting skill.

nodes.label: Postgres ACID Storage
nodes.rationale: Postgres is authoritative for relational data, ownership, append-only ledger entries, and idempotency.

nodes.label: ClickHouse Analytics Storage
nodes.rationale: ClickHouse serves historical and aggregate queries only so the live path remains independent of it.

nodes.label: Redis Ephemeral Storage
nodes.rationale: Redis can be flushed; it is not authoritative and non-state keys require TTLs.

nodes.label: Event Log
nodes.rationale: The Rust writer is isolated from the hot path so log lag can drop-and-count records in live mode.

nodes.label: DevOps Docker CI and Free Hosting
nodes.rationale: The deployment constraint is free to build and run, with a local-first design.

nodes.label: Market Microstructure Metrics
nodes.rationale: Rust computes metrics while Java forwards and Python/UI consume them, preventing independent cross-language recomputation.

nodes.label: Observability and Latency Measurement
nodes.rationale: Headline latency numbers must use same-clock measurements; cross-host figures are indicative only.

nodes.label: Order Book Engine Correctness
nodes.rationale: A book that might be wrong is marked Invalid and is never served as valid.

nodes.label: Paper Trading and Ledger
nodes.rationale: Trading is simulated only; ledger entries are authoritative and every account has one serialized writer.

nodes.label: Portfolio Presentation
nodes.rationale: Every published number needs a method and an exact benchmark-result directory.

nodes.label: Protobuf and gRPC Contracts
nodes.rationale: The proto is the single source of truth, and generated code must not be hand-edited.

nodes.label: Python Backtesting Engine
nodes.rationale: Backtests are conservative, reproducible claims; StateView prevents access to future data.

nodes.label: Realtime WebSocket Fan-out
nodes.rationale: One slow client must not slow other clients or grow memory without bound.

nodes.label: Rust Hot-Path Performance
nodes.rationale: Correctness never yields to a benchmark number; hot-path work is bounded and allocation-free.

nodes.label: Rust to Python with PyO3 and Maturin
nodes.rationale: A shared order-book implementation avoids drift between the live feed and backtests.

nodes.label: Security Hardening
nodes.rationale: Deny by default, centralize user isolation, and keep the platform paper-trading-only.

nodes.label: Testing and Quality
nodes.rationale: Goals are earned through deterministic replay, property/differential testing, and regression coverage.

nodes.label: Recorded Feed Fixtures and Golden Vectors
nodes.rationale: Fixtures are deliberately small and compressed; large recordings stay outside git.
